title: When the Inventory Sings
premise: Orsen Nystrom has spent twelve years writing postcards to a burned-down address, rehearsing confessions she never sends to the woman who left without goodbye. When her childhood home — the one that burned — goes up for auction, she returns to confront not only the house but the stranger in the old photographs: her mother's other daughter, raised elsewhere and now the estate's executor. As the sale deadline closes in, Orsen discovers the fire was no accident and that her mother chose survival over both daughters. In the end, Orsen lets the house go, forgives the dead woman who couldn't stay, and claims a found family with the sister she never knew.
about_author: Edmund Winterbourne is the pen name of a former estate auctioneer who spent two decades cataloguing the belongings of the departed. He writes quiet novels about the objects people leave behind and the words they never said.

chapters.title: Postcards to Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen Nystrom, a professional letter-writer for hire, mails another unsent postcard to an address that burned twelve years ago. Her POV establishes her ritual of almost-saying-it and her carefully ordered life. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine, cracked open when a legal letter arrives about the house auction.

chapters.title: The Executor
chapters.summary: At the county records office, Orsen meets Vera Lindqvist, the estranged half-sister handling their mother's estate — the stranger from the photographs. Told in alternating POV, each sizes the other up across a table of paperwork. Emotional beat: wary hostility masking recognition; they agree to prepare the house together, neither admitting why.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: First walkthrough of the charred house. Orsen catalogs salvageable items while flashbacks reveal her childhood there; Vera reveals she grew up knowing of Orsen but was forbidden contact. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through objects — a melted music box that still plays three warped notes.

chapters.title: Inventory of Almosts
chapters.summary: Sorting the mother's belongings, they find boxes of unsent letters addressed to both daughters, dated across decades. Orsen reads hers; Vera refuses to read hers. Emotional beat: the sisters' fault lines deepen as Orsen realizes their mother wrote to everyone except herself honestly.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Watched
chapters.summary: An elderly neighbor, Halvard, hints the fire started inside, not by accident, and that he saw someone leave that night. Orsen's POV spirals into suspicion; Vera dismisses it as senility. Emotional beat: dread replacing nostalgia — the house becomes a witness, not a wound.

chapters.title: Auction Preview
chapters.summary: The auctioneer previews the lot; strangers handle Orsen's childhood. A collector offers Vera cash to close early, pressuring the timeline. Orsen, POV, watches her history priced in lots. Emotional beat: humiliation and urgency — she must find the truth before everything is sold.

chapters.title: The Night It Burned
chapters.summary: Halvard produces a photograph: their mother leaving the house unharmed hours before the blaze, carrying one suitcase. Confrontation between sisters erupts — Vera accuses Orsen of mythologizing a woman who abandoned them both. Emotional beat: climax of resentment; the found family fractures before it can form.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsent
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Vera finally opens her own box of letters and learns their mother sent her away to protect her from a debt and a threat tied to the house itself — choosing survival over love, twice. Alternating POV converges. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuting into understanding; forgiveness begins as comprehension.

chapters.title: The Last Lot
chapters.summary: Auction day. Orsen stands to speak, publicly releases the house and its secrets, and bids nothing — instead giving Vera the music box and reading aloud the one postcard she never mailed. Emotional beat: catharsis; the art of almost saying it ends in finally saying it.

chapters.title: Where the Address Lives Now
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Orsen writes one final postcard — to Vera, at a new shared address. The house is gone; the family isn't. Epilogue-style dual POV shows them planting something where the foundation was. Emotional beat: resolution — love against duty resolved into love chosen freely, survival's price paid together.
